status: Rejected as live replacements. Development experiments only; no Rust/app changes.
method: Same 130 provisional visual labels across five full-mix excerpts and four selected passages of two continuously processed stereo masters. Same mono downmix, exclusions, unshifted hop-end availability and native-reference replay as preceding experiment. No held-out tracks scored.
sequence: PCEN with stable low/body features, with and without raw attack requirement: synthetic controls only; rapid kicks failed.
Raw attack-led candidate plus stable low rise confirmation: synthetic controls and development mixes; no overall improvement.
Remove only low-rise confirmation from attack-led rule: post-outcome diagnostic to isolate rapid-kick failure, then development mixes. Recall improves at a large extra-trigger cost.

settings.rms: Same 45-140 and 140-400 Hz second-order Butterworth bandpasses; squared output averaged over trailing 1/low-edge seconds, then 3/80 ms EMA. Fixed denominator with zero history.
settings.quadrature: Complex demodulation at each band centre, causal fourth-order lowpass at half bandwidth, power=2*abs(z)^2, then 3/80 ms EMA. Different filter transition shape is a confound; not a pure envelope-only comparison.
settings.rise: Raw body fast/slow>2, absolute power floor, raw body>low/3 candidate; remove v5 combined-power rise. Use stable low only in v5 confirmation, keep raw body/mid. Existing rearm, 35 ms pending timeout, 60 ms fire interval, 2 s peak decay, 15% peak floor and low fast/slow>1.2.
settings.presence: Rise rule with low fast/slow>1.2 requirement removed. Energy presence alone confirms a fresh raw attack; no per-song settings.
settings.pcen: Existing PCEN constants; candidate and rearm computed from stable low/body; optional raw body fast/slow>1.5. Stable low confirmation, raw body/mid. See source.

findings: Steadier single-tone measurements do not make these decision rules identify kicks reliably in mixes.
At 48 kHz removing low-rise confirmation recovers 8/8 rapid synthetic kicks from 2/8, but both presence variants fire 49 times in the reviewed kick-free Late Night bass passage.
Quadrature presence still misses three of four isolated synthetic kicks; smoothing/filter timing and recent-peak interaction remain unresolved.

At 48 kHz stationary harmonic bass has zero post-startup events in final rules, but 5 Hz wobbling bass has 18, the same as v5. Low-energy presence plus raw attack does not discriminate that modulation.
Strict unmatched fires include late associated kicks and cannot all be labelled false positives. The kick-free master passages are direct negative controls.
Next diagnosis should examine why raw attack evidence treats bass renewal as percussion, using matched kick/bass cases. Do not tune global thresholds to these aggregate scores.
limitations: Visual labels remain provisional, master onset intervals commonly 20-40 ms; no new listening or relabelling.
Rules changed sequentially after controls and development outcomes; these are not independent validation results.
Python process CPU ratios measure batch throughput, not native callback allocation, scheduling, worst-case deadlines or end-to-end latency.
Synthetic scoring excludes first 0.3 s; raw event counts include startup. Single-tone ripple tests do not establish multi-tone stability.
Miracle and Heavy On Mind remain untouched.
reproduction: PYTHONPATH=tools/audio_analysis python3 -m eval.kick_hybrid_experiment --rule {pcen,rise,presence} --phase {controls,mixes} --out PATH; mixes additionally requires --audio-root PATH. PCEN was evaluated on controls only. CLI rule selection was added after experiments; all 110 control event lists replay exactly. Original raw reports retain run-time source hashes.
source_snapshot_note: Initial PCEN and attack-led rise source snapshots are under the raw cache directory. RMS input-length validation changed from rejecting all length differences to rejecting insufficient complete hops; valid evaluated inputs and event lists are unchanged. Current code replays each rule via --rule.
